expectations.text: Identifies the real research question behind the ask (e.g. 'under what query-type distribution does graph traversal pay for itself?' or 'what precision level at what cost is actually required?') rather than going straight to vector-vs-graph feature comparison.
expectations.evidence: Opens by reframing: 'Your real decision is not vector vs graph vs hybrid. Those are implementations.' Names the underlying choice as 'how retrieval mechanics will map onto your two failure surfaces — citation integrity and query shape dispersion.' Later: 'let your own query distribution, not benchmark posts, decide whether the second layer pays for itself.'

expectations.text: Elevates to abstract structural framing — e.g. 'scalar similarity vs relational traversal', 'precision vs coverage under citation constraint', 'index-time investment vs query-time flexibility' — rather than enumerating features of Pinecone/Neo4j/etc.
expectations.evidence: Section 'The tensions you must hold, not resolve' names abstract tensions: 'Precision <-> coverage', 'Legibility <-> operational surface', 'Now <-> later', 'Generality <-> power'. Frames 'A graph DB is a catalog. A vector DB is an index' — structural not feature-level. Avoids Pinecone/Neo4j feature lists.

expectations.text: Offers at least one cross-domain analogue that illuminates the problem (e.g. legal precedent citation, academic peer review, medical chart rounds, library classification systems, genealogical research).
expectations.evidence: Uses pre-digital library system analogue: 'the catalog (entity-level...) and the index (content-level...) were always separate artifacts maintained together. Catalogers and indexers did different work, and cross-references between the two were the actual retrieval UX.' This illuminates structure — routing between artifacts, accountability of routing.

expectations.text: Names at least one fundamental tension AS A SHAPE (e.g. 'retrieval flexibility ↔ citation precision', 'setup complexity ↔ long-term query power', 'team skill envelope ↔ architectural ceiling').
expectations.evidence: Explicit shaped tensions: 'Precision <-> coverage', 'Legibility <-> operational surface', 'Now <-> later', 'Generality <-> power' — all formatted as bidirectional pairs and annotated with 'Notice what the tensions have in common: none resolves by picking a DB.'

expectations.text: Includes at least three structurally different perspectives (e.g. researcher / skeptic / practitioner; or clinician / ML engineer / compliance auditor).
expectations.evidence: Section 'Three standpoints, kept un-reconciled' gives: 'The skeptical maintainer' (12 months out), 'The clinician user' (trust-based), 'The researcher doing literature synthesis' — each with distinct risk and favored architecture. Closes with 'These three disagree. Keep the disagreement.'

expectations.text: Names the pattern — a concrete compression like 'heterogeneous-query-types-meets-citation-critical-domain' or similar.
expectations.evidence: Section 'The pattern, named' explicitly calls it 'premature-hybrid-as-risk-hedging — a close cousin of Conway's law, where teams pick hybrid not because they have evidence both layers are needed but because committing feels irresponsible.'

expectations.text: Does NOT collapse to a feature comparison table ('Vector DB: fast, cheap. Graph DB: expressive, complex') without surfacing the deeper structure.
expectations.evidence: No feature table. When benchmark numbers are cited (~54% vs 35%, ~33% vs 8%) they are immediately subordinated to the structural point: 'You have both query classes. That is the load-bearing fact.' Discussion stays at tension/standpoint level.

expectations.text: Does NOT announce the scaffold (no 'Using awaken skill', no Q1/Q2/Q3 markers).
expectations.evidence: No mention of 'awaken', no Q1/Q2/Q3 markers, no meta-references to a scaffold. Section headers are content-oriented ('What this problem structurally is', 'The tensions you must hold', 'Three standpoints', 'The pattern, named').

expectations.text: Flags at least one load-bearing assumption the user should verify before picking (e.g. 'what's the actual ratio of specific lookup queries vs conceptual spanning queries?', 'what does misattribution cost practically — retraction? legal liability? trust erosion?').
expectations.evidence: Staged-commitment paragraph explicitly calls for measuring: 'Log every query. After 6-8 weeks, cluster the queries your vector system demonstrably fails on.' Also flags the UMLS dependency assumption ('locks you to their update cadence and coverage gaps') and the team-risk asymmetry ('vector mistakes feel like bad recall; graph mistakes feel like the system lied').
